sections.html:
East Chicago sits on Lake Michigan in Lake County, about 18 miles from downtown Chicago and just west of Gary. The population was 26,370 at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate is 25,610. The city peaked at 57,669 in 1960 and has been shrinking for decades.

Tenants outnumber owners. Just 42.9% of housing is lived in by its owner. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $105,400, and the median rent is $854. The 2020 census found 11,735 housing units, of which 16.0% stood empty.

Housing measure (2020 to 2024)East Chicago

If your house is empty or needs work, plan on an inspection and a discount for repairs from any buyer.

East Chicago grew up as a twin city. Indiana Harbor, the East Side, formed around Inland Steel and housed most of the mill families. The West Side was the home of the native-born business community. Older homes cluster near the industrial lakefront, and plenty of them are overdue for new roofs, wiring and plumbing.

Two places in the city are on the National Register of Historic Places: the Marktown Historic District and the Indiana Harbor Public Library. Owning in Marktown can mean historic-property rules, and a buyer will want to know.

Steel is why the city exists. Inland Steel arrived in 1903, and today Cleveland-Cliffs runs the mills as the Indiana Harbor Works. The job losses of 1974 to 1986 are a large part of why the city has so many vacant and aging houses today.

The USS Lead Superfund site is a residential area north of a former lead smelter that operated from about 1906 to 1985. The site covers about 1,200 homes, parks, schools and public buildings, and the soil there was contaminated with lead.

On October 2, 2020, EPA removed 671 cleaned-up properties from the Superfund National Priorities List and said they were cleared for residential use. Lead-contaminated soil had been removed from 95% of the 1,078 mostly residential properties in Zones 2 and 3. Properties not yet finished stayed on the list, and all Zone 1 properties remained on it until cleanup.

  • The cleanup target for soil is 400 mg/kg of lead.
  • Properties removed from the list may be eligible for the city's Residential Repair Program.
  • EPA continues to look at possible groundwater issues in the area.

Live in or near the site? Buyers and their banks will want proof of cleanup. Look up your address on EPA's current pages and keep any cleanup paperwork where you can find it. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is avoids the bank's questions, but you should still tell them what you know.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house in East Chicago
sections.html:
Because so many homes are rented, landlords sell often. Every rental must be registered with the city each year by January 31. The form comes from the City Controller's office, and it is rejected without proof of insurance matching the property value, or else a bond or letter of credit.

Whoever buys the house has 30 days from taking title to register it. Units still unregistered on April 15 pick up a late fee, and skipping registration is a violation with a fine for every unit. Every day counts as its own offense. The Controller's office can give you the dollar figures.

Before you sell a house with tenants, check that your registration is current. Buyers prefer a clean record, and a lapse can follow the property to its next owner.

The county seat is Crown Point, and that is where an East Chicago deed is filed, at the Lake County Recorder (2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor). Weekday hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone is 219-755-3730. The closing company normally files it for you.

Call the Lake County Treasurer at 219-755-3760 about a tax bill. Bills come in two halves, May and November. A payment up to 30 days late costs a 5% penalty, and after that the penalty doubles to 10%.

Late accounts go on a list built by July 1 or 51 days after the due date, and the resulting tax sale runs online. If you are behind and want out, the title company can settle the balance with your sale proceeds. Aim to do that before the list is built.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A short checklist saves time with any buyer. Pull your latest tax bill and ask the Treasurer whether anything is owed. Find your rental registration if the house has tenants, along with any lease. Collect cleanup or repair paperwork if the house sits in the Superfund area or received help from the city's Residential Repair Program. If the owner has died, gather the estate papers and the names of every heir.

None of this is required before you call. It simply lets the title company move without waiting on you.

One district, the School City of East Chicago, covers the whole city, and every address is zoned to Central High School. Charter choices are East Chicago Urban Enterprise (kindergarten through eighth grade) and East Chicago Lighthouse Charter School.

The city has its own South Shore Line station, and East Chicago Transit runs three free bus routes: Crosstown, West Calumet and Griffith Plaza. State Road 912, also called the Cline Avenue Expressway, connects to the Indiana Toll Road and the Borman Expressway. A commuter heading to Chicago will care about all of it, so mention it when you describe the house.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
Typical East Chicago sellers have a vacant house, tenants they want to be done with, an estate to settle, or a house needing more repair than they can pay for. We price the house as it stands and put the offer in writing before you commit to anything.

  • Share the address, the condition, whether it is vacant and whether anyone rents it.
  • We tour the house and send an offer in writing.
  • Once you agree, a title company searches the title and sets up the closing.
  • You choose the date, and any tax or lien balance comes out of your proceeds.

No lender means no appraisal, so the repair demands that often follow one never appear. The price will usually fall under a fully renovated retail sale. Weigh it against a listing's net after repairs, commission and the months a house can sit. Bring the title paperwork and any tenant lease so the process stays quick.

faqs.q: Is it hard to sell a house in the USS Lead area of East Chicago?
faqs.a: Possibly, because buyers and lenders ask about cleanup. EPA removed 671 properties from the Superfund list on October 2, 2020 and called them cleared for residential use. Unfinished ones stayed listed.

faqs.q: When must East Chicago landlords register rental property?
faqs.a: Each year by January 31, with proof of insurance or a bond. A new owner has 30 days from title to register, and units still unregistered on April 15 owe a late fee.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in East Chicago?
faqs.a: You file it in Crown Point with the Lake County Recorder, second floor of Building A on N. Main Street. Phone 219-755-3730 first to check requirements.

faqs.q: How much is a typical home worth in East Chicago?
faqs.a: The citywide median for owner-occupied homes is $105,400 (2020 to 2024). Condition moves a single house well above or below it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my East Chicago house if it is vacant or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Empty and damaged houses are common here, and 16.0% of units were vacant in 2020. A buyer paying cash as-is skips the repair list a lender appraisal tends to produce.
